x-bow: clock 2:44: he identifies the archetype instantly and rates the matchup - "dude, this guy is X-Bow... X-Bow's going to be a pretty solid match-up for us. I do feel like that if he plays perfectly, he can make the match a little bit tight" (730-747s).

The opponent's X-Bow only shows at (2, 16) at clock 0:55, 0:17 and in overtime, always too late to matter.
tesla: clock 2:39 onward: the opponent's Tesla, not the X-Bow, is what Ryley plays around - "I'm going to make sure that I play all of my cheapest cards that I can, so I can cycle back quickly, and try to out-cycle that Tesla, cuz forcing him to go for a defensive X-Bow would be really, really good" (773-783s). At clock ~1:04 he declares the plan complete: "We did outcycle him" (836s).

overtime: he treats a forced Tesla as a win either way - "if I make him Tesla then he can't really activate the king" (887-890s), and later spends a spell on it, "just to make sure we drop the Tesla. Or if he puts it on the side then that's fine, too" (912-915s).

bullets: Win by out-cycling, not by out-damaging: against an X-Bow/Tesla siege player he states the plan at 773-783s - "I'm going to make sure that I play all of my cheapest cards that I can, so I can cycle back quickly, and try to out-cycle that Tesla" - and confirms it landed at clock ~1:04, "We did outcycle him" (836s). Opponent conceded in overtime with his right tower at 1,037 hitpoints (931-934s).

The offence is one repeated shape: Hog Rider at the right bridge (16, 14-15) at clock 2:12, 1:28, ~1:07, ~0:48, ~0:11 and twice in overtime, with Evolved Firecracker or Evolved Skeletons trailing and The Log cleaning up - "as long as we get the Hog Rider shots on the tower, man, that's all I really care about" (858-861s).

The defence is centre-column Evolved Cannon plus Mighty Miner in front of the King Tower: Cannon at (4, 13), (9, 11), (8, 10), (8, 11) and Mighty Miner at (9, 0), (7, 8), (2, 4). Placement is chosen to deny the siege - "cannon high could be better... he can't do like a high defense. He'd have to put everything low" (787-794s) and "mighty miner in the middle here, in front of my king tower. He can't X-Bow on the left" (795-799s).

Earthquake is the answer to the defensive building the cycle plan forces out: cast on the Tesla at clock 1:25 as a deliberate overspend ("I know I can overspend here and get away with it", 812-815s), as X-Bow bait at clock 0:21 ("go for the Earthquake to bait him into going for an expo", 870-875s), and behind the Hog in overtime ("just to make sure we drop the Tesla", 910-913s).

Ryley rates the archetype as favoured into X-Bow and credits the small spell for it - "with perfect game play, Hog Rider should be winning, especially with the log. Having log to keep up with the tower damage" (749-754s). Title of the video: "NERF the Hog Rider NOW!!!"

Deck note: the eighth slot is Earthquake, not the Heal Spirit the HUD reported (mean hand confidence 0.509). He narrates his own Earthquake three times (812s, 870-875s, 910-913s) and six of seven Earthquake events land on the opponent's half; that makes this the standard Hog Earthquake cycle list, seven cards shared with the KB's "Hog MM EvoCannon 2.6 Cycle" deck.

new_deck.rationale: A 2.6-cost-style Hog Rider Earthquake list whose plan is explicitly to spend only cheap cards and cycle the win condition faster than the opponent can pay for a defensive building.
new_deck.why_it_works_md: The deck is built around getting Hog Rider to the bridge more often than the opponent can afford an answer: six of its eight cards cost 1-3 elixir, so a Cannon-plus-Skeletons defence still leaves the cycle intact. Ryley's stated plan against siege is to "play all of my cheapest cards that I can, so I can cycle back quickly, and try to out-cycle that Tesla, cuz forcing him to go for a defensive X-Bow would be really, really good" (773-783s). Earthquake closes the loop: whatever building the cycle forces out gets broken behind the next Hog, which is how he treats the Tesla at clock 1:25 and again in overtime. Defensively an Evolved Cannon placed high in the centre column plus Mighty Miner in front of the King Tower covers both lanes and denies X-Bow placements, while Evolved Firecracker and Electro Spirit clear the ranged cycle troops siege decks lean on. The Log converts repeated Hog connections into a tower: "Having log to keep up with the tower damage, for the most part, is very, very nice" (749-754s).
